# Bitsocial Chain

> BSO is the money of Bitsocial, the peer-to-peer social network that no company owns. An Ethereum L2 appchain where communities own their networks, their tokens and their revenue.

Use `https://chain.bitsocial.net/` for the official BSO and Bitsocial Chain landing page. The current immutable BSO token is live on Ethereum; the Bitsocial Chain L2 and later roadmap phases are proposed infrastructure unless the page explicitly says otherwise.

## Landing page

- [Bitsocial Chain home](https://chain.bitsocial.net/): The missing social layer of crypto. Crypto became a casino because Web2, TradFi, and centralized infrastructure own the distribution rails and bend the incentives. Bitsocial Chain fixes this: an unstoppable, fully decentralized Ethereum L2 appchain where communities own their networks, their tokens and their revenue.
- [Why a Chain](https://chain.bitsocial.net/#why-a-chain): Why does a peer-to-peer social network need a chain? Bitsocial itself is not on a blockchain. Posts, profiles, communities and moderation on Bitsocial are peer-to-peer. No chain, no fees, no wallet: you can use the whole network without ever touching crypto, and most people will. But a few things genuinely need a chain — names that are yours, money that moves between strangers, tokens a community actually owns. Bitsocial Chain is for exactly those, and nothing else.
- [Why an L2](https://chain.bitsocial.net/#why-an-l2): Why an Ethereum L2 instead of a new blockchain? Ethereum already does the hard part. A new blockchain would rebuild what Ethereum already provides: the security and the developer base. Bitsocial only needs a small set of on-chain functions on top, and an appchain does those few things well while keeping Ethereum underneath.
- [Tokenomics](https://chain.bitsocial.net/#tokenomics): What are BSO's tokenomics? Sound money. BSO is a fixed-supply ERC-20: 210 million, no inflation, deflationary by design. The whole supply was airdropped, with no presale and nothing carved out ahead of the community. Its contract is immutable and adminless, so the rules are fixed forever.
- [The Airdrop](https://chain.bitsocial.net/#the-airdrop): Who got BSO? Was there a presale? Airdropped, never sold. Around 600 people, in January 2022. They registered through a Telegram bot that gave each of them a referral code, and bringing in more people earned a larger allocation. Every recipient was then checked by hand, specifically so that no one could walk away with too much of the supply.
- [Unstoppable](https://chain.bitsocial.net/#unstoppable): Who runs the chain? Can it be shut down? No operator, no off switch. Every action on Bitsocial Chain is a plain Ethereum transaction, sent to an address nobody controls. Nodes read Ethereum's history and apply the same open rules, so every node arrives at the same state, and anyone could rebuild it from Ethereum alone. No company sits in the middle to pressure, and there is nothing to switch off.
- [BSO Names](https://chain.bitsocial.net/#bso-names): What happens to my .bso name? Your .bso name stays yours. Bitsocial apps resolve .bso names today by borrowing ENS, the naming system Ethereum wallets use: mycommunity.bso is really mycommunity.eth carrying a bitsocial record. A native registry would airdrop every name already in use to the wallet that holds it — nothing to claim and nothing to re-register.
- [Community Money](https://chain.bitsocial.net/#community-money): What would communities do with it? One asset under many communities. Each community would run its own layer — an L3 — with its own token and its own shared pot of money, while paying its fees in BSO. L3s already exist across crypto, but they mostly host the same trading as everything underneath them. On Bitsocial Chain one would arrive with a community already attached, which is the part crypto has never had.
- [Ads and Tips](https://chain.bitsocial.net/#ads-and-tips): How would communities make money? Revenue burns at the point of sale. One way it could work: a community auctions its ad slots through a contract, advertisers bid in the community's own token, and part of every sale is destroyed on settlement while the rest goes to the community. No sales team, no treasury and no buyback bot, so there is no pot for anyone to capture. Only revenue born on-chain can be programmed like this, and none of it is scheduled.
- [Privacy](https://chain.bitsocial.net/#privacy): Will everyone see who I tip? Tipping shouldn't dox you. Bitsocial Chain is public by default, like Ethereum, and .bso names are meant to be seen. Money is different: a tip should never require putting your name, profile or post on-chain beside it, and a fresh wallet should be normal, not suspicious. The chain won't build its own privacy system. It is designed so existing ones can plug in without asking permission: shielded pools, stealth addresses, zero-knowledge proofs.
- [Possibilities](https://chain.bitsocial.net/#possibilities): Is it live? What's planned? Proposed, in the open. Not live yet. BSO is live on Ethereum today; Bitsocial Chain is a proposal, and its first proof of concept, native .bso names, runs on a test chain. Nothing below has a date. It is what a social layer with its own money would make possible: some of it will get built, some replaced by better ideas, and some built by people who have not shown up yet.
- [Verify](https://chain.bitsocial.net/#verify): How do I get BSO safely? Only one address is BSO. Anyone can create a token and call it BSO, so the contract address is the only thing that tells the real one apart. Match all 42 characters against this site and Bitsocial's official channels before sending anything anywhere.

## Official docs

- [Bitsocial Chain](https://docs.bitsocial.net/bitsocial-network/): Phase 2 architecture and economic-layer overview.
- [BSO Token History](https://docs.bitsocial.net/token-history/): Verifiable history of BSO and its immutable Ethereum contract.
- [Bitsocial Chain proof of concept](https://github.com/bitsocialnet/bitsocial-chain#readme): Working .bso name registry derived from Ethereum L1 history, with its stated limitations.
